messages:
ken (eng-releases): quick idea — proposal for a tiny command + preflight template to speed up safe rollouts. thinking of a 'fastpin' flag for the deploy bot and an auto-generated release-notes stub.

sara (release-eng): yes pls. current flow is a lot of manual copy/paste for change windows + notes. can we also include a small healthcheck script that the bot runs post-canary? :+1:

jamie (sre): would prefer the bot to gate on two signals: 1) canary success % (from perf checks) and 2) synthetic healthcheck response time. if either fails, auto-rollback. we should keep the rollback command short.

deploy-bot: I can add a new command: `/deploy fastpin --ver <version> --window "<start>-<end>" --notes-template` returns a dry-run summary. example usage: 
```
/deploy fastpin --ver v2026.03.01 --window "2026-03-21T02:00Z/2026-03-21T03:00Z" --canary 5% --notes-template
```

ana (product): (typo: ana) the notes-template could pre-fill sections: summary, risk, rollback-plan, postmortem-checks. that will help PMs and support triage.

lee (oncall): for change windows, can we have the bot reject if it overlaps with an existing major window? we keep hitting overlap when multiple teams schedule. bot could query calendar or a simple internal calendar endpoint.

ken (eng-releases): agreed. rough plan:
1) add `/deploy fastpin` that does: pin the version, create a minimal release note stub, schedule the change window, start canary at requested %
2) run two automated checks (perf gate + healthcheck) for the canary window
3) if gate fails -> bot issues `rollback --auto` with short reason and notifies channel

ken (eng-releases): sample preflight YAML the bot will accept (one-liner in chat):
```yaml
preflight:
  canary_pct: 5
  healthcheck: "/internal/health?svc=api&timeout=2000"
  perf_metric: "p50_latency_ms"
  perf_threshold_ms: 250
  rollback_on: ["healthcheck_fail","perf_regression"]
```

sara (release-eng): love the structured YAML. suggest adding `notify_on` so ops and product get pinged during canary. also a field `auto_rollback_delay_s` so we don't flip too quickly on transient blips.

jamie (sre): +1. also want a tiny shell snippet for the healthcheck step that teams can customize:
```bash
# run synthetic request and return "ok" when healthy
resp=$(curl -sS -m 2 https://canary.${SERVICE_HOST}/health)
if [[ "$resp" != "ok" ]]; then
  echo "healthcheck_fail"
  exit 2
fi
```

deploy-bot: implemented dry-run output for `/deploy fastpin --dry-run` like: 
- pinned version: v2026.03.01
- window: 2026-03-21T02:00Z/2026-03-21T03:00Z
- canary: 5%
- checks: healthcheck (/internal/health), perf p50 < 250ms
- notifications: #eng-prod-alerts, @sara, @jamie

ana (product): please ensure the release-notes stub includes the change window and a checklist (preflight, smoke, validate later). also add a generated changelog link to the commit range.

lee (oncall): question: how does pin interact with existing pins? e.g., customer has dedicated pipeline pinned to model X. can the bot warn when the pin is incompatible?

ken (eng-releases): good call. bot will check for active pins and surface a soft-warning with `--force` opt-in. default: abort if incompatible.

sara (release-eng): one small UX ask: the bot should create a one-click rollback in the thread so engineers can hit a button in Slack to rollback if someone manually observes an issue. could be a `rollback` button that expands to confirm.

jamie (sre): and record the rollback reason automatically to the release notes template (selectable quick reasons: perf, error-rate, infra).

ken (eng-releases): implementation milestones: 1) add command + dry-run, 2) accept preflight YAML and parse logic, 3) add auto-rollback + notifications, 4) release notes auto-stub + one-click rollback. target: next sprint.

deploy-bot: note: calendar API requires team token. please add `eng-releases-calendar` service account to infra-iam.

lee (oncall): i'll create a tiny playbook entry for the one-click rollback flow and add it to runbook.

ana (product): can we also scaffold a `rn-gen` helper that converts commit range + PR titles into the notes section? make it optional.

ken (eng-releases): yes — `rn-gen` will be an opt-in subcommand: `/deploy rn-gen --range abc..def` -> returns a list of bullets you can edit before publishing.

sara (release-eng): sounds great. i'll sketch the preflight YAML editor and a minimal template for the release notes and drop it in the repo. tagging for follow-up: @jamie for healthchecks, @lee for calendar access, @ana for RN fields.

jamie (sre): cool. if no objections i'll start PR for the healthcheck gating and a tiny simulation harness so we can test rollback behaviour locally.

ken (eng-releases): thanks everyone. let's keep this lightweight — prefer iteration. i'll open an umbrella RFC and link it in here when ready. :rocket:
